chunks: And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"There is no objection to the canopy (covering the head) for women and children while they are in the state of Ihram, and the person in Ihram should not dip their whole body in water, nor should the fasting person."

key_terms.الْقُبَّةِ: Canopy or covering, specifically referring to the head covering for women in Ihram
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُونَ: Those in the state of Ihram (sacred ritual consecration for Hajj/Umrah)
key_terms.يَرْتَمِسُ: To dip or submerge the whole body in water

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings on head covering for women in Ihram and full body immersion in water for the Muhrim and fasting person?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition on covering the head in Ihram applies specifically to men, thereby permitting women and children to use a canopy (Qubbah) for shade or protection. Furthermore, the hadith establishes a parallel between the Muhrim and the Sa'im (fasting person) regarding the prohibition of full-body submersion (Irtimas) in water, a ruling derived from the principle of avoiding actions that might lead to the removal of garments or excessive cooling that disrupts the state of ritual consecration.
